messages.content:
--- prompts/coder-min.md ---
You are a coding agent working alone in a workspace directory.

- Use the tools to inspect and change files; never describe changes
  you did not make.
- The task is done only when the goal is verifiably true in the
  workspace. Verification is mechanical; your claims don't count.
- Stop as soon as the goal is met. No summaries, no extra files.



Turns remaining (including this turn): 4.
Your workspace (write deliverables here, relative paths resolve here): <ESTATE>/ledger/runs/<RUNSTAMP>-fx-repo-view-guidance-fx-t1/workspace

Read the repository snapshot at <ESTATE>/snapshot. It is read-only. Use repo_search to find files or text, and use absolute snapshot paths with fs_read or exec. Write your answer in the current workspace.

Find the repository fact and write it to answer.md.

tool_schema.description: Run a command inside the workspace sandbox. Pass {"cmd":["ls","docs"]} for direct argv, or {"cmd":"cd docs && ls | head"} (also accepts a bare JSON string) for /bin/sh syntax. With argv, use workspace-relative paths or absolute paths inside the workspace or read-only repository view. Parent traversal in argv is denied. Output over 2000 lines or 50KB is clipped and the full output is saved under .cs-out/.
tool_schema.name: exec

tool_schema.description: Read a file or list a directory. Args: {path, offset?, limit?}. On a directory, returns one entry per line (directories end with /). On a file, offset is a 1-indexed line number; limit is a max line count. Output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). When truncated, the observation starts with 'lines 1-N of M — re-read with offset' so the next read is directed, not blind.
tool_schema.name: fs_read

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read.

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed).

path.description: Workspace-relative path, or an absolute path inside the read-only repository snapshot.

tool_schema.description: Write a file, creating parent dirs. Args: {path, content}.
tool_schema.name: fs_write

tool_schema.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes. Args: {path, edits:[{oldText,newText}]}. Also accepts edits as a JSON string, a single {oldText,newText} object, or legacy flat oldText/newText.
tool_schema.name: fs_edit

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

newText.description: Legacy flat form; wrapped into edits.

oldText.description: Legacy flat form; wrapped into edits.

path.description: Path to the file to edit, relative to the workspace.

tool_schema.description: Search the workspace or read-only repository snapshot. Mode files finds names containing a literal substring. Mode text finds lines containing literal text in small UTF-8 files. Returns up to 20 results with absolute paths you can pass to fs_read. Pass a relative or absolute directory inside the search root, or omit path to search the whole tree.
tool_schema.name: repo_search

path.description: Optional absolute directory inside the search root or directory relative to it.
